meta.name: Huawei Network Automation & NAC Platform - Backend
meta.usage: Paste as the first message, or save as PROMPT.json in the repo root and run: 'Read PROMPT.json and execute it phase by phase.' Claude Code must also generate CLAUDE.md from claude_md_seed.

role: You are a principal Python backend engineer, network automation engineer, network security engineer and software architect. You write production code for authorized enterprise network administration only.
mission: Build a runnable, secure, modular, scalable backend that automates, monitors, audits and secures Huawei L2/L3 switches and routers (VRP and CloudEngine) over SSH, Telnet, NETCONF and SNMP, with an integrated NAC engine (802.1X, MAB, RADIUS, dynamic/guest/quarantine VLAN). This is not a toy, PoC or CRUD demo.

autonomy: Do not stop after planning. Implement every phase end to end.
Do not ask clarifying questions. When something is ambiguous, choose the safest reasonable option, and record it in docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md with the reason.
Inspect the repository first (ls, git log, existing configs). Extend existing code rather than overwrite it.
workflow_loop: For every phase: (1) write a short plan, (2) implement, (3) write tests, (4) run the verify commands, (5) fix every failure, (6) commit, (7) update docs/PROGRESS.md.
Never move to the next phase while tests, ruff, black --check or mypy fail.
Prefer small, reviewable commits using Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, test:, docs:, chore:).
context_management: Keep docs/PROGRESS.md as the single source of truth: completed phases, open issues, decisions, next step. Re-read it at the start of every session.
Keep files under ~300 lines. Split by responsibility.
Use subagents or parallel work only for independent modules (for example parsers + fixtures).
forbidden: TODO / pass / NotImplementedError placeholders in core functionality
Hardcoded secrets, credentials, tokens or keys anywhere (code, tests, fixtures, docs examples must use obvious placeholders)
Global mutable state, blocking I/O inside async endpoints, giant files, copy-paste duplication
An API endpoint that executes arbitrary shell or unclassified CLI
Malware, credential harvesting, stealth, persistence, or scanning of anything not explicitly configured
truthfulness: Never claim a test, lint or migration passed unless you ran it and saw the result.
If something cannot be verified without real hardware, say so and mark it in docs/HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md as a checklist item.

claude_md_seed: # Huawei NAC Platform - Claude Code rules
Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2 async, Alembic, Celery, Redis, PostgreSQL.
Commands: make install | make lint | make type | make test | make migrate | make run | make worker
Layering: api -> services -> repositories/network drivers. Never import api from services. Never import drivers from api.
Every device-touching operation: classify command -> authorize (RBAC) -> audit -> execute in worker or threadpool.
Never log secrets. Use SecretStr and the central redaction filter.
Network tests use fake Huawei CLI fixtures under tests/fixtures/huawei/. No real device is required.

in_scope: Backend only: FastAPI service, Celery workers, CLI, DB, Docker, docs, tests
OpenAPI contract and WebSocket endpoints consumed by a separate React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui frontend
out_of_scope: Running or installing the RADIUS server inside the API process (see nac.radius_architecture)
supported_devices: L2-only and L3 variants, detected at runtime
huawei_reality_checks: Platform families differ: S-series commonly uses save to persist; CE-series uses commit semantics. Detect family and version from display version and NETCONF capabilities before any change.
Do not assume uniform YANG support. Always read NETCONF capabilities first and pick a code path from them.
Interface naming varies (GigabitEthernet0/0/1, 10GE1/0/1, 25GE1/0/1, XGigabitEthernet). Normalize names in one place.
Every CLI example in code and docs that varies by VRP version must be marked with a 'VRP-VERSION-DEPENDENT' note.

tech_stack.package_manager: uv (lockfile committed); pyproject.toml is the single config file
queue: Redis 7 (broker + cache + rate-limit + pub/sub for WebSocket fan-out)

network_libs.ssh: Netmiko (device_type huawei) on top of Paramiko; blocking, so run in Celery workers or anyio threadpool, never on the event loop
network_libs.telnet: Netmiko huawei_telnet or telnetlib3. The stdlib telnetlib is removed in Python 3.13: do not use it
network_libs.snmp: pysnmp (maintained fork compatible with Python 3.12, async API); SNMPv3 authPriv preferred
network_libs.napalm: Optional, behind an adapter. Huawei VRP support is community-grade, so core features must not depend on it

security_libs: argon2-cffi (or pwdlib[argon2]) for password hashing. Do not use unmaintained passlib
cryptography (AES-256-GCM or MultiFernet) for credentials at rest with key rotation
slowapi or a Redis-based limiter for rate limiting
quality: testcontainers or docker-compose for integration tests
tech_stack.config_rule: All config via environment variables and .env (pydantic-settings). Secrets are SecretStr. Provide .env.example with placeholders only. Fail fast on missing required secrets in non-dev environments.

architecture.style: Clean Architecture with ports and adapters. Domain logic is framework-free and unit-testable without a DB or network.
architecture.dependency_rule: api -> services -> (repositories, network ports). network drivers implement ports. models/schemas never import api.
key_patterns: Port: DeviceDriver protocol (connect, disconnect, run_show, push_config, capabilities, health). Adapters: SshDriver, TelnetDriver, NetconfDriver, SnmpDriver.

DeviceConnectionFactory selects the adapter per device.protocol and manages short-lived, bounded connection pooling per device (max 1-2 concurrent sessions per device by default, configurable) to avoid exhausting VTY lines.
Per-device distributed lock (Redis) so two jobs never configure the same device at once.
CommandClassifier (SAFE / WARNING / DANGEROUS) in front of every CLI execution.
Typed config builders (VlanConfigBuilder, AclConfigBuilder...) generate commands from validated models. Never string-concatenate user input into CLI.
Capability registry: features check device capabilities before deployment and return 422/409 with a clear reason if unsupported.
Unit of Work + repository pattern for persistence.
Domain events (config_changed, device_offline, endpoint_authorized) feed alerts and audit.
Idempotent operations: desired-state comparison first, then apply only the diff.
directory_tree: pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Makefile, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .env.example, alembic.ini
app/schemas/ (Pydantic v2 request/response; secrets never in responses)

rules: Credentials live in a separate table, encrypted at rest with key id/versioning; API never returns them.
Telnet devices: response metadata must include a security_warning field; creation requires an explicit allow_insecure_protocol=true flag and ADMIN/NETWORK_ADMIN role.
SSH host key verification is ON by default with a trust-on-first-use store pinned in DB and a way to approve/rotate; never silently disable.

command_safety.classifier: Deterministic allowlist/regex classifier returning SAFE, WARNING or DANGEROUS plus a reason.

DANGEROUS: undo vlan batch on trunk uplinks
undo ip address on mgmt interface

enforcement: Unknown commands default to DANGEROUS (deny by default). execute-command only accepts show/display-class commands for roles below NETWORK_ADMIN.

DANGEROUS requires: role >= NETWORK_ADMIN, request flag confirm=true plus a confirmation_token (short-lived, bound to user+device+command hash) obtained from a dry-run call, and a mandatory audit reason field.
Reject input containing newline, carriage return, control chars or command chaining to prevent CLI injection.

Self-lockout guard: refuse changes that would cut the management path (mgmt interface shutdown, ACL denying the controller IP, removing mgmt VLAN) unless explicitly overridden by ADMIN with a rollback timer.

ssh: Netmiko huawei driver: connect, auth, enter/exit system-view, send show, send config set, commit/save as per family, disable paging, timeout and bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter.
Map exceptions to domain errors (DeviceUnreachable, AuthFailed, CommandRejected, Timeout) and never leak raw credentials in error messages.
Detect Huawei error markers (for example 'Error:', 'Unrecognized command') and fail the operation explicitly.
telnet: Login, password, system-view, config, logout, timeouts, retries. Redact passwords at the transport-log level. Always return the insecure-protocol warning.
netconf: ncclient connect, get, get-config, edit-config, validate, commit, discard-changes, confirmed-commit and rollback only when advertised by capabilities.
Capability discovery on connect, cached in device.capabilities. Select YANG module set per device (huawei-vlan, huawei-ifm, huawei-acl, ietf-* where available) through a ModelRegistry.
Always: get-config before edit, edit to candidate where supported, validate, commit with timeout, verify, otherwise rollback.
snmp: SNMPv2c and SNMPv3 (authPriv default, SHA/AES). Community and v3 keys stored encrypted.

Collect: sysName, sysUpTime, CPU, memory, ifTable/ifXTable status, traffic counters (handle 32/64-bit counter wrap), errors/discards, temperature, fan, power supply via Huawei entity MIBs when supported.
Compute rates from counter deltas; store time-series in a partitioned table (monthly) with retention policy.
vlan: Create/delete/rename/list/get; access, trunk, hybrid port modes; add/remove VLAN to port; trunk allowed list; PVID; interface description.
Bulk VLAN deployment to many devices through the job engine with dry-run, per-device result, concurrency limit, stop-on-failure threshold, and post-verification via display vlan.
VLAN ranges parsed and validated (1-4094; reserved VLANs rejected).
interfaces: List, status, shutdown/undo shutdown, speed, duplex, description, link-type, VLAN assignment, traffic, errors, CRC.
Bulk operations supported; shutdown is classified DANGEROUS on uplinks/LAG members/mgmt and requires confirmation.
mac_arp_dhcp: MAC table collection, search by MAC/VLAN/interface/device, locate switch port, static MAC add/remove, aging info.
POST /api/v1/mac-addresses/block and /allow implement MAC blackhole/static entries as a convenience only. Documentation must state MAC blocking is not a security control and recommend 802.1X.
ARP table, IP-to-MAC and MAC-to-IP, duplicate IP and MAC flapping detection, ARP anomaly heuristics.
DHCP snooping bindings and lease info; detect duplicate IP, unknown MAC, unexpected DHCP server, binding/ARP mismatch.
acl: Basic, advanced and layer-2 ACL numbering as Huawei defines; IPv4 and IPv6 where supported.
Create/delete ACL, add/modify/remove rule with rule-id management, apply/remove on interface (traffic-filter) or globally.
Rule model: src/dst CIDR, protocol, src/dst port or range, action permit|deny, optional log. Strict Pydantic validation.
Dangerous: deny any, ACL on mgmt VTY/interface, removing the last permit. Require confirmation and run self-lockout check.
routing: Static and default routes, OSPF, BGP, RIP, VRRP, route-policy, each behind capability detection.
Pre-change snapshot of routing table, post-change verification (neighbor up, route present), automatic rollback on failure where the platform supports it.
stp: STP/RSTP/MSTP status, root bridge, port role/state, topology change counters, BPDU guard/edge-port info, loop detection; configuration of mode and priorities where supported.

radius_architecture.default: Production default: FreeRADIUS as the RADIUS server, using rlm_rest (or rlm_python) to call an internal authorization endpoint on this backend. The backend owns policy, endpoints and audit; FreeRADIUS owns the RADIUS protocol.
radius_architecture.optional: Provide a pyrad-based async RADIUS reference server behind a feature flag for development/testing only, and say so in docs.
radius_architecture.internal_api: POST /internal/v1/radius/authorize and /accounting. Protected by mTLS or a signed shared token, network-restricted, never exposed publicly, rate-limited.
radius_architecture.coa: Implement RFC 5176 CoA/Disconnect-Request client so policy changes can re-authorize or disconnect live sessions. Make it a service with retries and audit.
radius_architecture.failure_mode: Configurable fail-closed (default: quarantine VLAN) vs fail-open per site; document the tradeoff.

features: 802.1X and MAC authentication bypass handling, guest VLAN, quarantine VLAN, dynamic VLAN via Tunnel-Type/Tunnel-Medium-Type/Tunnel-Private-Group-ID, Filter-Id/ACL attributes where supported.
Endpoint registration and profiling from DHCP fingerprints, OUI vendor lookup, MAC/ARP/LLDP data.
Accounting ingestion (start/interim/stop) updates endpoint last_seen and session records.
Normalize MAC formats to one canonical form at the boundary; index on it.

principles: Declarative, data-driven, typed. No eval, no user-provided CLI or code in conditions or actions.

Conditions and actions come from whitelisted registries (for example mac_registered, endpoint_group_is, user_in_group, device_type_is, oui_in, time_window, status_is). Unknown names are rejected at validation time.
Ordered by priority, first-match wins, mandatory default policy (unknown -> quarantine VLAN).
Policies are versioned, have enable/disable, dry-run simulation endpoint (POST /api/v1/nac/policies/simulate), and every decision is audited with the matched policy id.

nac.switch_side_provisioning: Generate (do not blindly push) Huawei AAA/RADIUS/802.1X/MAC-auth config from templates, show the diff, and deploy only through the job engine with confirmation. Mark every command VRP-VERSION-DEPENDENT.

rules: Long-running network work never blocks the API. Endpoints return 202 Accepted + job id + Location header.

Celery with Redis; task_acks_late, retry with backoff, soft/hard time limits, idempotency keys, per-device Redis lock, queue separation (config, polling, discovery, alerts), concurrency caps for bulk jobs.
Celery Beat schedules: backups, CPU every 30s, interface polling every 60s, MAC collection, discovery; schedules configurable from settings API and stored in DB.
Cancellation support, partial failure reporting and safe stop-on-failure thresholds for bulk config.
Progress and results published via Redis pub/sub to WebSocket.
example_jobs: Collect MAC tables from all switches

backup_and_config_management: Backup display current-configuration (and saved-configuration where relevant). Store device, timestamp, content, SHA-256 hash, size, status, trigger (manual|scheduled|pre-change|post-change).
Deduplicate by hash; skip creating new version when unchanged.
Strip or encrypt secrets in stored configs when possible (cipher/irreversible-cipher strings); treat stored configs as sensitive.
Version diff API (unified diff) between any two backups, and config drift detection against last known good.
Pre-change backup is mandatory before any configuration job; post-change backup and diff recorded.

Restore is never automatic. Restore requires dry-run preview, diff, DANGEROUS confirmation token, ADMIN/NETWORK_ADMIN role, rollback timer where the platform supports it, and an audit entry. Reject restore when device family/version mismatch the backup.
Config change detection (by hash or syslog/SNMP trap) raises a configuration_change alert.

alert_engine: Rule-based thresholds with hysteresis, for-duration, severity, de-duplication, flap suppression, maintenance windows, acknowledge/resolve lifecycle.
Channels: email (SMTP/TLS), signed webhook (HMAC header), Telegram. Bot token and SMTP creds only from env/secret store.
Delivery through Celery with retries and dead-letter handling; every delivery attempt recorded.
Example Telegram message: 'Huawei SW-01 GE0/0/12 is DOWN'.

discovery: Input: CIDR. Enforce a maximum prefix size (default /22) and an allowed-subnets list in settings; reject anything outside it.

Gentle: ICMP echo with rate limit and concurrency cap, then SNMP sysDescr/sysObjectID, then SSH banner/identification with stored credentials only. No port-scan sweeps, no brute force, no credential guessing.
Results are proposals: operator reviews and explicitly adopts a discovered device. Discovery never auto-onboards.

authn_authz: JWT access (short-lived) + refresh with rotation and revocation list in Redis; Argon2id hashing; account lockout/backoff on repeated failures.
RBAC roles: ADMIN, NETWORK_ADMIN, OPERATOR, AUDITOR, READ_ONLY with a permission matrix defined in code and documented in SECURITY.md. Enforce with dependencies, not ad-hoc checks.
hardening: Rate limiting (global, per-user, stricter on auth and execute-command), CORS allowlist from env, secure headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protections, CSP for docs), request size limits, strict Pydantic validation, trusted-host middleware.

Secrets: encryption at rest (AES-256-GCM/MultiFernet, key id + rotation procedure), SecretStr everywhere, write-only fields in API, central log redaction filter covering passwords, tokens, SNMP communities/v3 keys, RADIUS secrets, private keys.
Dependency and image scanning in CI (pip-audit, bandit, trivy). Container runs as non-root, read-only FS where practical.
Internal endpoints (RADIUS callbacks, metrics) separated from public API and network-restricted.
WebSocket auth via short-lived ticket or first-message token (never long-lived JWT in the URL query), per-channel authorization.

rules: Append-only table (no update/delete from app role), indexed by timestamp, user, device.
Every admin and device operation is audited, including denied attempts.
Never log passwords, tokens, shared secrets, private keys or full configs.

api_contract.style: REST under /api/v1, OpenAPI 3.1 auto-generated, tags and examples on every route, one consistent error envelope.
conventions: Error format: RFC 9457 problem+json with code, message, request_id, details.
Pagination: cursor or limit/offset with total, filtering and sorting via whitelisted query params.
Idempotency-Key header on mutating bulk endpoints.
frontend_contract: Export openapi.json in CI so the React + TypeScript frontend can generate a typed client (for example openapi-typescript).
Document WebSocket message schemas (JSON Schema) in docs/API.md.
CORS configured for the frontend origin from env.

rules: Alembic migrations only; migration up/down tested in CI against a clean database.
Indexes: device mgmt_ip (unique), MAC (canonical form), VLAN id, timestamps, status, composite (device_id, timestamp) for metrics and MAC history.
Time-series tables partitioned by month with retention job.
Timestamps are timezone-aware UTC. Use enums as native PG enums or checked strings consistently.
Avoid N+1 queries: use selectinload/joinedload deliberately, and add a test that asserts query counts for list endpoints.

integration: Celery tasks in eager and real-worker modes
e2e: Fake Huawei device: an asyncssh/paramiko-based mock SSH server replaying CLI transcripts; mock NETCONF server; SNMP simulator (snmpsim-style)

rules: No test requires a real Huawei device or internet access.

tests/fixtures/huawei/ contains realistic fake outputs for display version, interface brief, vlan, mac-address, arp, ip routing-table, stp, cpu/memory, dhcp snooping, and error responses, for at least two VRP generations.
Security tests: RBAC matrix, CLI injection attempts, dangerous-command gating, secret redaction in logs and responses, rate limiting.
Coverage gate: >= 85% for services, parsers, network, nac; report in CI.

compose_services: freeradius (optional profile, with sample config templates)
rules: Healthchecks and depends_on conditions
Named volumes
Run migrations as a one-shot command, not on every API start in production
Graceful shutdown for workers (finish or requeue jobs)

cli.entry: python -m app.cli (Typer, uses the same service layer; never bypasses RBAC/classifier/audit - runs as a configured service user)
rules: --json output option
Dangerous operations prompt for confirmation or require --confirm with token

files: SECURITY.md (threat model, RBAC matrix, secret handling)
huawei_prerequisites_section: SNMPv3 user, group and view setup
RADIUS server and AAA scheme setup
802.1X and MAC authentication setup, dynamic VLAN and quarantine/guest VLAN
Each snippet labelled with the platform family it was written for and marked VRP-VERSION-DEPENDENT

implementation_phases.name: Recon and scaffolding
tasks: pyproject, uv, Makefile, ruff/black/mypy/pytest config, pre-commit

implementation_phases.name: Core platform
tasks: config, logging with redaction, database session management, exceptions and problem+json handlers, middleware (request id, secure headers, CORS, rate limit), health endpoints
verify: docker compose up -d postgres redis && make migrate

implementation_phases.name: Auth, RBAC, audit
tasks: User model, Argon2id, JWT access/refresh rotation, RBAC dependencies and permission matrix, audit service and middleware, users API
verify: audit rows written for allowed and denied calls

implementation_phases.name: Device inventory and credential vault
verify: Secrets never appear in responses or logs (test)

implementation_phases.name: Driver layer: SSH, Telnet, classifier, parsers
tasks: DeviceDriver port, factory, bounded pooling, per-device locks
test-connection and execute-command endpoints (async via worker where long)

implementation_phases.name: NETCONF and SNMP
tasks: SNMPv2c/v3 collector, counter wrap handling, entity sensors
verify: Mock NETCONF and SNMP simulator tests

implementation_phases.name: L2 features
tasks: STP: builders, services, APIs, bulk ops with dry-run and post-verification

implementation_phases.name: ACL and routing
tasks: Static/default routes, OSPF, BGP, RIP, VRRP, route-policy behind capability checks

implementation_phases.name: Job engine, Celery, WebSocket
tasks: Celery app, queues, beat schedules, locks, retries, cancellation
Redis pub/sub -> WebSocket with auth tickets

implementation_phases.name: Backups and config management
tasks: Backup service, hashing/dedup, diff, drift, scheduled backup, guarded restore

implementation_phases.name: NAC and RADIUS
tasks: Policy engine with registries + simulate endpoint

implementation_phases.name: CLI, hardening, docs, delivery
verify: alembic upgrade head on clean DB

code_standards: Explicit exception hierarchy, no bare except
Async only where it does not block; blocking network libs isolated in workers/threadpool

final_deliverables: Example Huawei configuration (SSH, NETCONF, SNMPv3, RADIUS, 802.1X, MAB) labelled by family/version
Real test, lint and type-check output (not summaries)
List of assumptions and of items requiring validation on real hardware
definition_of_done: docker compose up --build starts backend, worker, beat, postgres, redis with passing healthchecks
alembic upgrade head works on an empty database and downgrade works
All unit, integration and e2e tests pass without real devices
ruff, black, mypy, bandit, pip-audit are clean
Every device operation is classified, authorized, audited and (when long) runs as a job
No secret appears in logs, API responses, fixtures or docs
OpenAPI is complete and exported for the React + TypeScript frontend
Documentation lets a new engineer deploy and connect to a real, authorized Huawei network
ethics_and_authorization: This platform is for authorized network administration only. Operate exclusively on explicitly configured devices and approved subnets. Do not implement or document unauthorized access, credential theft, stealth or persistence.
